read: Compare only after normalising for non-PO mix. A low figure with high non-PO share is a process problem, not a people problem
Below 80% means most spend bypasses the control that makes matching possible, and everything downstream gets manual
The strongest single predictor of AP effort. Above 15% the team is running a rework function, not a payment function
Raw process speed, independent of payment terms. Anything above 5 days usually points at approval routing, not capacity
Read against agreed terms, never on its own. High DPO with low paid-on-time means late payment, not working capital management
The headline AP service metric. Below 60% is almost always an approval bottleneck rather than a deliberate cash decision
Cheque volume carries cost, delay and fraud exposure. Usually the cheapest win available and rarely contested
A long tail of terms makes on-time payment unmeasurable, so fix this before trying to improve the paid-on-time number
Directly quantifiable missed savings. Low capture alongside slow cycle time is the clearest cost-of-delay argument available
Normalise the monthly query count against invoice volume before comparing. High query load usually tracks late payment, not vendor behaviour
